title: Beyond Moscow: Regional Growth Opportunities in Russian E-Commerce in 2026
excerpt: Russian e-commerce growth is shifting beyond Moscow. 2026 data on regional sales, warehousing, inventory and Wildberries/Ozon strategy for global brands entering Russia.

blocks.text: For years, Moscow dominated the conversation about e-commerce in Russia. 2026 data shows the market can no longer be read through Moscow and St. Petersburg alone.

Kokoc Group's analysis of 21 categories on Wildberries and Ozon shows regional clusters outside Moscow account for 73.7% of turnover. Moscow and Moscow Region share fell from 26.1% to 23.4% between June 2025 and July 2026.

blocks.title: For global brands
blocks.text: Russia marketplace strategy cannot rely on «ship stock to Moscow and wait». Read demand by region, allocate inventory from sales data, and evolve logistics as you scale.
Why is demand shifting to the regions?

Russia's geography creates both friction and opportunity. In many cities where offline retail offers limited assortment, marketplaces give access to a range comparable to Moscow. AKIT notes online share of retail can exceed Moscow's in Siberia and the Far East; in H1 2026, 45 regions were above the national average of 22.2% online share in retail.

No — Moscow remains Russia's largest single e-commerce market (~15.4% of national online trade in H1 2026). What changed is the assumption that Moscow alone represents all of Russia. Regional clusters should be treated as distinct demand pools.

items: Moscow Region, St. Petersburg, Krasnodar, Sverdlovsk, Rostov among top volume shares
Several regions saw ~30%+ YoY growth (e.g. Tuva, Dagestan, Kaliningrad, Amur)
Current volume and growth rate must be analysed separately

blocks.text: What this means for brands entering Russia

The classic path — Moscow warehouse → Wildberries/Ozon → nationwide sales — can work at launch. As volume grows, brands must track regional orders, SKU performance by region, delivery times, stockouts, overstock and returns. Inventory management becomes part of sales management. See [e-commerce logistics in Russia 2026](/en/blog/rusyada-e-ticaret-lojistigi-2026).
Central stock vs regional marketplace inventory
The goal is not to abandon central stock — it is to run central stock together with regional marketplace placements.

items: Central pool → controlled first placement on WB/Ozon → SKU/region analytics → transfers → scale new regions when demand is proven

blocks.text: Related: [Wildberries warehouse strategy](/en/blog/wildberries-depo-stratejisi-basarili-satis), [WB & Ozon logistics](/en/blog/wildberries-ozon-lojistik-yonetimi-stok-stratejisi), [Selling on Wildberries](/en/blog/wildberriesde-satis-yapmak), [Selling on Ozon](/en/blog/ozonda-satis-yapmak).
Wildberries and Ozon need separate regional plans
Warehouse networks, customer geography, category strength and fulfillment costs differ. The same SKU may need different placement on each platform.

Russia is a multi-centre e-commerce ecosystem, not a one-city market. Success requires the right geographic stock plan — not only the right product.
